text:
alexa: Quick sync — we want to launch a small UX experiment on the pricing page this Friday. Goal: clarify tier boundaries + make the cost calculator actually usable for infra teams. Keeping it lightweight, 2-week run.

mohit: 👍 can you share the exact changes? curious about the FAQ updates too.

alexa: Plan: 1) Rename tiers from "Core / Pro / Enterprise" to "Developer / Production / Dedicated" (try to signal latency/isolation). 2) Add short bullets under each tier: SLA, data isolation, typical throughput (tokens/s). 3) Replace current calculator with simplified inputs: monthly requests, avg tokens/request, percent cached.

sam: love the new names — they map to our product modes. but can we A/B test naming vs copy change only? want to know if names drive MQLs or just clarity.

tia: +1 to AB test. Also propose we add one FAQ item: "Which tier is best for regulated data?" with a 1-line answer pointing to Private. That should reduce inbound filtering to Support.

jordan: For calculators: I mocked a tiny input set. Example snippet (for dev to drop in):
```
{
  "monthly_requests": 200000,
  "avg_tokens": 400,
  "cache_hit_rate": 0.35
}
```
Outputs: est monthly tokens, est monthly cost (hosted), and recommended tier: if cache_hit_rate < 0.5 and monthly tokens > 50M -> Suggest "Production" or "Dedicated".

mohit: That logic seems fine — can you add a toggle for "private deployment" that highlights additional fees? Sales told me that's a common blocker.

alexa: Good call. We'll add a small CTA that says "Estimate private deployment" which opens a lead form (prefill calculator inputs).

marketing-bot: Reminder: experimental copy must be staged in staging by 09:00 PT Thursday for legal & privacy review.

tia: Who owns the FAQ text change? I can write the short Q/A if someone can review.

alexa: tia you own FAQ copy. sam can you set up the A/B test in Optimizely and configure goal events (calculator CTA clicks, MQL form submits)?

sam: On it. I'll wire events: calculator_open, estimate_private_click, form_submit. Sending draft dashboard later today.

jordan: I'll hand off the calculator React widget to eng by EOD. Implementation notes in the PR: localize numbers, round estimates, and show a small "accuracy margin" note.

mohit: Also add a small analytics event for "faq_read" so we can see if the new FAQ reduces contact-us clicks.

alexa: Nice. Final ask: can we route form submissions from the calculator to the inbound-sales queue with a tag "pricing-calc-experiment" so sales can prioritize?

sam: Yup — I'll add the routing rule and set up a Slack webhook to sales-channel for high-value estimates (> $50k).

tia: I'll drop the FAQ draft in this thread shortly.

alexa: Thanks everyone — plan: stage Thursday, launch Friday morning PST. We'll reconvene next Wednesday for a quick results sync. :rocket:
